# Results — Study 636 (Exchange-Listing-Pop)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — the
**"Coinbase effect"**: a coin pops double digits when Coinbase announces its listing, then
gives it all back — rebuilt on **129 Coinbase listing events 2019–2026**, priced on the
**Binance tape** (the coins trade there long before Coinbase lists them). Day 0 per coin = the
first daily candle of its USD product on Coinbase Exchange, from Coinbase's own public API.
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-07-02** (last complete UTC day; the youngest event is ≥ 35 days old so every +30
window is complete). Fingerprint `f6a046325f17`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | Binance USDT spot daily klines (public, keyless) — 134 event coins + BTC, **3,242 days**, 2017-08-17 → 2026-07-02 (8.9 years) |
| Events | **129** Coinbase listings (hardcoded table in [`data.py`](../exchange_listing_pop/data.py); day 0 = first Coinbase Exchange USD candle, fetched once 2026-07-03), all with full **[−20..+30]** coverage, in **95 same-day clusters** |
| Era split | **56** events before the 2022-04-28 "listing roadmap" policy, **73** after |
| Abnormal return | coin daily log return **minus BTC** (market-adjusted, β = 1) |
| Execution / costs | ONE lag: the listing goes live during day 0 → the follower's first fill is the **day-0 UTC close**; costs one-way × NAV per leg (10/25/50 bps), shorts pay borrow (10%/yr alt, 3%/yr BTC; sensitivity to 100%/yr) |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** The universe is Coinbase-USD products **whose
> candle history Coinbase still serves** ∩ Binance-USDT pairs with ≥ 60 days of pre-listing
> history. Binance serves klines for pairs it later delisted (ANT, OMG, MULTI, OOKI … are in
> the panel — the softener), but events on coins whose *Coinbase* candle history is no longer
> served, or that never had a Binance USDT pair, are absent. Five 2018–20 assets whose first
> Coinbase book was USDC-quoted (BAT, ZEC, CVC, DNT, MANA) are excluded because the USD-product
> date would mis-date the event. A mis-dated residual event would *dilute* the measured effect,
> not create it.

## The event windows — BTC-adjusted CARs (cluster-level one-sample *t*)

| window | mean CAR (log) | simple | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| early run-up [−20..−6] | +2.40% | +2.43% | +1.25 |
| **run-up [−5..−1]** | **+10.23%** | +10.77% | **+5.91** |
| listing day [0] | +0.77% | +0.77% | +0.82 |
| **THE POP [−5..0]** | **+11.00%** | **+11.63%** | **+5.74** |
| post [+1..+5] | −6.14% | −5.96% | −3.93 |
| **THE FADE [+1..+30]** | **−17.45%** | **−16.02%** | **−5.73** |

*(n = 95 clusters / 129 events per row.)* Both halves of the folklore are on the tape, at
5–6 sigma: an **+11% pop** into the listing and a **−17% give-back** over the next month —
the fade more than swallows the pop. The pop lives almost entirely in **[−5..−1]** — the
announcement-to-listing gap — while the **listing day itself is +0.77% (t = 0.82)**: by the
time the coin actually trades on Coinbase, the move is over.

## Inference — placebo + coarser clustering + hit rates

Placebo: same coins, random pseudo-listing dates ≥ 90 days from the true event; empirical *p*
of the mean CAR and a Welch *t* of event CARs vs the pooled placebo windows.

| window | event-level mean | Welch *t* vs placebo | placebo *p* (2,000 draws) | 20-seed *p* range |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| POP [−5..0] | +14.60% | **+6.92** (vs 188,947 windows) | **< 0.0005** | 0.0000–0.0000 |
| FADE [+1..+30] | −16.79% | **−4.38** (vs 185,676 windows) | **< 0.0005** | 0.0000–0.0000 |

| window | month-clustered *t* (n = 56) | median cluster CAR | clusters > 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| POP [−5..0] | **+5.30** | +7.11% | 76% |
| FADE [+1..+30] | **−4.96** | −17.97% | 19% |

Not an outlier artefact (median ≈ mean, 76% of pop clusters positive) and not a
time-clustering artefact (collapsing to 56 calendar months keeps *t* ≈ 5).

## Era split — the 2022-04-28 "listing roadmap" natural experiment

After the DOJ insider case, Coinbase started pre-announcing listings on a public roadmap
(2022-04-28), front-loading the news by weeks.

| era | POP [−5..0] | *t* | FADE [+1..+30] | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| pre-roadmap (37 clusters) | **+17.17%** | +5.52 | −16.98% | −3.95 |
| roadmap era (58 clusters) | **+7.06%** | +3.06 | −17.76% | −4.23 |

Pop difference pre-vs-roadmap: **Welch *t* = +2.61** — transparency **halved the pop** (it
now leaks out over the weeks between roadmap post and listing), but the **fade is untouched**
(−17% in both eras).

## Tradability — the follower's trade (enter at the day-0 close, ONE lag)

**Riding the pop is impossible after the fact.** Long the new listing / short BTC (hedged;
3%/yr borrow on the BTC leg):

| hold | cost (one-way) | gross | *t* | net | *t* | hit |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| +5d | 10 bps | −4.58% | −2.59 | **−5.03%** | −2.84 | 19% |
| +5d | 25 bps | −4.58% | −2.59 | **−5.63%** | −3.17 | 17% |
| +5d | 50 bps | −4.58% | −2.59 | **−6.63%** | −3.74 | 14% |
| +30d | 10 bps | −11.97% | −3.92 | **−12.61%** | −4.13 | 18% |
| +30d | 25 bps | −11.97% | −3.92 | **−13.21%** | −4.33 | 18% |
| +30d | 50 bps | −11.97% | −3.92 | **−14.21%** | −4.66 | 18% |

**Fading it is the trade.** Short the new listing / long BTC from the day-0 close, +30d:

| cost (one-way) | gross | *t* | net (10%/yr borrow) | *t* | hit |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | +11.97% | +3.92 | **+10.74%** | +3.52 | 79% |
| 25 bps | +11.97% | +3.92 | **+10.14%** | +3.32 | 76% |
| 50 bps | +11.97% | +3.92 | **+9.14%** | +3.00 | 75% |

Borrow sensitivity (25 bps, +30d): **+10.14% (t = +3.32)** at 10%/yr → **+6.86% (t = +2.25)**
at 50%/yr → **+2.75% (t = +0.90)** at 100%/yr. The edge is real at realistic large-cap borrow
and **dies exactly where borrow on a hot, freshly-listed alt actually lives** (thin margin
pools, 50–300% APY spikes, or no borrow at all) — the binding constraint is access to the
short, not the signal.

*(Untradable reference: the pop itself, CAR[−5..0] = +11.00%, t = +5.74, accrues **before**
the first close you can trade.)*

## Third axis — announcement vs listing: is the tradable part gone before you can act?

Documented announcement → first-trade gaps (Coinbase blog, per-row sources in
[`data.ANNOUNCEMENTS`](../exchange_listing_pop/data.py)): MATIC 2021-03-09 → 03-11 (2 days),
ADA 2021-03-16 → 03-18 (2 days), DOGE 2021-06-01 → 06-03 (2 days), SOL 2021-05-20 → 06-17
(28 days, delayed); since 2022-04-28 the public roadmap front-loads the news by **weeks**.

The tape's answer: the pop is **+10.23% in [−5..−1]** (t = +5.91) — i.e. inside the
announcement-to-listing gap, before Coinbase users can even buy — the **listing day adds
+0.77% (t = 0.82)**, and from the first close anyone can act on it is **−6.14% by +5 days**
and **−17.45% by +30**. The tradable part is gone **before** you can act: **CONFIRMED**.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

Deterministic panel, staggered pseudo-listings, a plantable pop (−2..0) and fade (+1..+20):

| planted | CAR[−5..0] | *t* | CAR[+1..+30] | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| pop 0%, fade 0% (null) | +0.41% | **+0.21** | +2.89% | +0.70 |
| pop 15%, fade 10% | +15.41% | **+7.71** | −7.11% | −1.73 |

The null stays quiet; the planted pop is recovered at its true size. *(Machinery proof only —
never cited in support of a stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** Both halves of the Coinbase effect clear the bar decisively on 129
  events: pop **+11.00%** (cluster *t* = **+5.74**, month-clustered *t* = +5.30, placebo
  *p* < 0.0005 across 20 seeds) and fade **−17.45%** (*t* = **−5.73**) — the give-back
  exceeds the pop. Survivorship named (Coinbase-served candle histories; delisted Binance
  pairs are in, mis-dated events would only dilute).
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The folklore's actionable half is worse than a mirage: buying at
  the first tradable close loses **−12.6% net** (t = −4.1) in 30 days. The *mirror* trade —
  short the fresh listing / long BTC — nets **+10.1% per event** (t = +3.3) at 25 bps and
  10%/yr borrow and still +6.9% (t = +2.25) at 50%/yr, but **dies at 100%/yr** (+2.8%,
  t = 0.9) — and hot new listings are exactly where borrow is thin, expensive or absent.
  Real edge, borrow-bound and short-only: FRAGILE, not INVESTABLE.
- **"Gone before you can act?" — CONFIRMED.** +10.23% of the +11% pop accrues in [−5..−1],
  inside the announcement-to-listing gap; the listing day itself is +0.77% (t = 0.82); the
  roadmap-transparency era **halved** the pop (+17.17% → +7.06%, Welch *t* = +2.61) by
  leaking it earlier still. Whatever the announcement is worth, it is priced before the first
  moment you can trade on Coinbase.
